scenes.name: Girl groups y Shangri-Las
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Antes del beat, el estilo de los grupos femeninos dominó las listas americanas desde que las Shirelles llegaron al número 1 con «Will You Love Me Tomorrow» (1961): discos afilados, bailables y bien observados. «My Boyfriend’s Back» de las Angels y «You Don’t Own Me» de Lesley Gore eran declaraciones chocantes. Tras la invasión británica, los Shangri-Las de Red Bird lo prolongaron un par de años: chicas duras de Queens a las que George «Shadow» Morton dejaba ser ellas mismas en sinfonías de 45 rpm con gaviotas y motos, sobre romances condenados y tragedias familiares, «como la chica corriente». Su último single en Red Bird, «Past, Present and Future» (mayo de 1966), sobre la «Sonata Claro de luna», es un examen desolado de un desastre amoroso.

podcast.title: First Meeting with Phil Spector
podcast.body: Her initial encounter with Phil Spector was fraught with tension; Spector, displaying erratic behavior, repeatedly left her office, looked at himself in a mirror, and adjusted his appearance while she attempted to play a song intended for The Paris Sisters, leading to her blunt confrontation and the loss of the sale. "Eventually she said to him, listen to me you little prick, did you come to look at yourself or to hear my songs? And she didn't make that sale."

podcast.title: Prominent Demo Singer
podcast.body: Before becoming a successful songwriter, Ellie Greenwich was recognized as one of the most important demo singers in New York, lending her voice to many potential hit songs. "She'd become one of the most important demo singers in New York, and it also started writing songs."

podcast.title: Second Meeting with Phil Spector
podcast.body: Despite Spector arriving four hours late, this second meeting, during which Spector was seemingly unaware he was meeting someone he had already made a poor impression on, led to a successful collaboration. Spector had become interested in a song she had sold to Aaron Schroeder and set up the meeting to discuss her writing for him. "That second meeting, which Specter didn't realise was with someone he'd already made a bad impression on, Specter turned up four hours late."
